To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the MEFV curves of patients with obstructive lung disease are simulated best by models with high small airway resistance and low lung compliance.

the MEFV curves of normal and obstructive subjects are similar in shape and differ only in magnitude; that the shape of the MEFV is independent of airway resistance and compliance, and depends only on the shape of the airway pressure-volume (APV) curve; and that the magnitude of the MEFVs is dependent on the magnitude of the APV curve and the compliance and resistance of the airways.
The shape of the maximum expirory flow-volume curve is determined by the ratio of airway resistance to airway compliance and by the ratio of lung compliance to airway compliance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an analog computer simulation of the human ventilatory system.
the development of a model of the ventilatory system that is useful in the diagnosis of pulmonary diseases.

the development of an analog computer simulation of the pulmonary system which will allow us to investigate the effects of various pulmonary diseases and the effects of various therapeutic measures on the MEFVs and other pulmonary functions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper presents a new and simpler model for the simulation of the MEFV maneuver.
the MEFV test is a sensitive test for the diagnosis of airway obstruction.
the analog simulation of the MEFV maneuver provides a simple, inexpensive, and accurate tool for the diagnosis of pulmonary disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MEFV test is a useful tool for the diagnosis of obstructive and restrictive airway disease.

the analog computer simulation of MEFV curves is a powerful tool for studying the effects of changes of the model parameters on the shape of the MEFV curves and for comparing these effects with those of clinical observations.
the analog computer is an excellent tool for studying the effects of changes of various parameters on the MEF-V curve.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the model structure presented here can be used to simulate a wide range of pulmonary function test maneuvers, including those that are difficult to simulate on a digital computer.
the model structure presented here may be used as a basis for a digital simulation of the MEFV test.
the analog computer is a useful tool in the study of the respiratory system.
